records.title: OpenAI TTS (gpt-4o-mini-tts, tts-1, tts-1-hd)
records.summary: OpenAI's text-to-speech models behind /v1/audio/speech, with built-in voices and an instructions field on gpt-4o-mini-tts. All three models are deprecated with a shutdown date.
records.why_it_matters: Many skills and scripts call this endpoint for narration; they stop working on 2027-01-06 and the named successor uses a different API.
records.status_note: Deprecated; OpenAI's TTS guide gives a shutdown date of 2027-01-06 (read 2026-11-12).
records.fit_notes: Do not start a new pipeline on it: migration goes to gpt-realtime-2.1-mini on the Realtime API, which is not a drop-in for /v1/audio/speech. Until then use wav or pcm for video sync (pcm is 24 kHz 16-bit with no header). The page says 11 built-in voices in its intro and 13 in the voice list. Per-minute or per-character price was not read here. Usage policy requires telling listeners the voice is AI.

related.note: The speech skill still defaults to gpt-4o-mini-tts.

claims.text: tts-1, tts-1-hd and gpt-4o-mini-tts shut down on 2027-01-06; the successor is not supported on /v1/audio/speech.
claims.quote:
The tts-1, tts-1-hd, and gpt-4o-mini-tts models are deprecated and will
shut down on January 6, 2027. Migrate to gpt-realtime-2.1-mini using the
Realtime API. This is a change of API workflow:
gpt-realtime-2.1-mini isn’t a supported model for /v1/audio/speech.
claims.locator: Text to speech guide, deprecation notice at the top

claims.text: OpenAI's usage policies require a clear disclosure that the voice is AI-generated.
claims.quote:
Our usage policies require you
to provide a clear disclosure to end users that the TTS voice they are hearing
is AI-generated and not a human voice.

claims.text: OpenAI recommends marin or cedar for best quality.
claims.quote: For best quality, we recommend using marin or cedar.
claims.locator: Text to speech guide, Voice options

checked.what: OpenAI text-to-speech guide (deprecation notice, voice options, output formats, usage-policy note) against the claims

records.title: Gemini TTS (Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS)
records.summary: Google's text-to-speech models on the Gemini API, with prebuilt voices, style control through turn metadata and inline tags, and two-speaker dialogue in one request.
records.why_it_matters: It is the cheapest first-party hosted narration with a price on the page, and the price doubles on 2027-01-01.
records.fit_notes: Paid output is $9 per 1M audio tokens ($0.00225 per 10 s) through 2026-12-31 and $18 from 2027-01-01; budget with the 2027 number. The free tier exists but its data is used to improve Google products; use the paid tier for client scripts. Gemini 3.8 returns full WAV with a 44-byte header; strip it or request audio/l16 before joining turns. Voice design, remixing and replication features exist; replication is cloning and out of scope here; use prebuilt voices. No SynthID statement was found on the TTS page.

claims.text: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS output costs $9.00 per 1M audio tokens through 2026-12-31 and $18.00 from 2027-01-01.
claims.locator: Pricing page (markdown), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, Standard tab, Output price

claims.text: Google equates the 2027 output price to $0.0045 per 10 seconds of audio.
claims.locator: Pricing page (markdown), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS, Standard tab, Output price

claims.text: Joining separately generated turns needs raw PCM or the WAV header stripped.
claims.quote:
Because unary requests return `audio/wav` with a 44-byte RIFF header by
  default, request raw PCM (`{"type": "audio", "mime_type": "audio/l16"}`) or
  strip the WAV header from each turn before concatenating the 24kHz PCM
  audio frames.
claims.locator: Speech generation guide (markdown), Limitations, second bullet

checked.what: Gemini API speech-generation guide (markdown) and Gemini API pricing page (markdown), Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS section, against the claims

records.title: Stable Audio Open
records.summary: Stability AI's open-weight text-to-audio models. Stable Audio Open 1.0 makes up to 47 seconds of 44.1 kHz stereo from a text prompt and is stronger on sound effects than music. Stable Audio 3 checkpoints exist on Hugging Face behind a gate.
records.why_it_matters: It is the local route to generated sound effects and ambience for a clip, under a licence that allows commercial use below a revenue line.
records.fit_notes: Weights are gated: a Hugging Face login and accepting the licence form are needed before download, so an agent cannot fetch them unattended. Commercial use is free under USD 1M annual revenue; above it an Enterprise licence is needed. Outputs belong to the user. Keep clips under 47 s per generation and plan crossfades for longer beds. No Mac path is documented on the 1.0 card; mlx-audio lists Stable Audio 3 MLX ports, whose card was not read here.

related.note: ACE-Step is stronger for songs; Stable Audio Open for effects.

claims.text: Stable Audio Open 1.0 generates up to 47 seconds of 44.1 kHz stereo audio.
claims.quote: Stable Audio Open 1.0 generates variable-length (up to 47s) stereo audio at 44.1kHz from text prompts.

claims.text: The card says it is better at sound effects and field recordings than music.
claims.quote: The model is better at generating sound effects and field recordings than music.

claims.text: The Community License allows commercial use for individuals and organisations under USD 1M annual revenue.
claims.quote: The Stability AI Community License allows for research, non-commercial, and commercial use of the Core Models for individuals or organizations that generate under $1M (or local currency equivalent) of annual revenue, regardless of the source of that revenue.

checked.what: stable-audio-open-1.0 model card page, stability.ai/license FAQ and the Stability AI Community License Agreement page against the claims; the stable-audio-3 card was gated and not read

records.title: MusicGen and AudioGen (AudioCraft)
records.summary: Meta's AudioCraft library with the MusicGen text-to-music and AudioGen text-to-sound models. Code is MIT, weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.
records.why_it_matters: Older guides still suggest MusicGen for a soundtrack; its weights licence is non-commercial, which rules it out for monetised or client video.
records.fit_notes: Use only for drafts or internal tests. For a commercial clip use model:ace-step/ace-step (output stated usable commercially) or model:stabilityai/stable-audio under its revenue threshold. Mac support and output-ownership terms were not checked here.

claims.text: The code is MIT but the model weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.
claims.quote: The models weights in this repository are released under the CC-BY-NC 4.0 license

claims.text: The weights licence file is the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 text.

checked.what: facebookresearch/audiocraft README License section and LICENSE_weights against the claim
